messages.text: Searched the web · Harlo OS web flasher error "Failed to execute 'open' on 'Ser
Handed to the team · Flasher fails at the serial open step on a known good port; cannot verify the er

Hi Andrew,

Your attachment did not come through on this end, so I am working without the wording of the error. I am not going to guess at what it says, but there is one cause that fits your symptoms exactly, and it is worth trying before anything else.

The error appearing a second or two after you pick COM3, rather than when you plug the module in, is the signature of the port being opened and then refused. On Windows that almost always means something else already has COM3 held open. The usual culprits are a second browser tab with the Harlo flasher still loaded from an earlier attempt, a serial monitor or terminal window, Arduino IDE, or any vendor tool that auto connects. A tab you flashed from before counts even if you think you left it. So: unplug the module, close every browser window completely, close anything else that talks to a serial port, then reboot the PC. After the reboot, open one single Chrome window, go to the Harlo site, plug the module in, and only then select COM3. If the flasher offers an erase or a slow baud rate option, take the slower one.

If that still fails, the next most likely cause is the USB to serial driver rather than the flasher. COM3 showing in Device Manager tells us a driver is loaded, but not that it is a good one. Expand Ports in Device Manager, right click the COM3 entry and look at the driver name and version. If it is a CH340 or a CP210x, download the current driver straight from WCH or Silicon Labs, install it, reboot and try once more. An old or Windows supplied CH340 driver enumerates fine and then fails on open, which is exactly what you are seeing.

For whoever picks this up next, the detail that matters most is the exact text of the error, so please send the screenshot again as a plain image attachment, or simply type out the line word for word along with the driver name and version from Device Manager. With that I can match it to the right fix instead of working from the shape of the problem.

I have put this in front of JD, our hardware lead, with everything you have already tried. He picks it up today from 10am Eastern and the answer comes back to you here by email. If you would rather not wait, he is very active in our Discord at (contact hidden), and the Harlo OS channel there is full of people who have flashed this exact module. Posting the error screenshot there often gets an answer within minutes.

Hal
Searched the web · esptool "Invalid head of packet (0x45)" possible serial nois
Searched the web · Harlo OS web flasher LilyGo T-Display "Invalid head of packe
Handed to the team · Follow-up to the earlier technical flag: the exact error text has now arrived, s

Hi Andrew,

That text is the piece I was waiting for, and it changes the picture. 
"Invalid head of packet (0x45): Possible serial noise or corruption" is not the Harlo site's own wording, it comes straight out of esptool, the Espressif flashing engine the web installer runs underneath
. So this is a standard ESP32 flashing error rather than anything specific to the BC04, which is good news because it is well understood.

What it actually means: the flasher sent its first command down the port and the module answered with something that was not a valid reply packet. The 0x45 is the first byte it got back, and 0x45 is the ASCII letter E. In other words the chip was talking normally, printing its boot log, instead of sitting in download mode waiting to be programmed. 
Espressif's own answer on the same error is that it comes down to the chip not being held in the bootloader properly, or the data on the line being corrupted
. It is nothing to do with radio interference, despite how the message reads, and nothing to do with your miner.

So the fix is to get the module genuinely into download mode and keep the link clean. The button timing matters more than I suggested before. Unplug the USB from the module. Press and hold the BOOT button and keep holding it, then plug the USB in while it is still held, count three, and only then let go. The screen should stay dark or blank, which is what download mode looks like. Now go to the Harlo page, pick the Hammer BC04 profile, select COM3 and start. Do not press RST at any point in that sequence. If it still throws the same error, repeat it but tap RST once while BOOT is still held down, then release RST, count one, then release BOOT.

Two things that help the link itself. Plug into a USB socket on the back of the PC, directly on the motherboard, not a front panel port, not a hub and not an extension lead, because a hub is a common cause of exactly this corruption. And if the flasher gives you any choice of speed or baud rate, take the slowest one offered, usually 115200. A high baud rate on a marginal lead produces this same garbled first byte.

One more thing worth knowing. If the first attempt partly wrote something before failing, the module can come back up in a confused state and keep failing until it is put in download mode by hand, which is what the sequence above does. So do not be put off if it took several goes.

I have passed the exact error text to JD, our hardware lead, along with everything you have tried. He picks this up today from 10am Eastern and you will get his reply here. If you want it sorted sooner, he is in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf as @nullhashrate, and the Harlo OS channel there has people flashing these modules daily.

Hal

Hi Andrew,

No rush at all, enjoy your day out.

When you do get to it, the only thing I would ask is that you tell me which of the two button sequences you used and what the screen on the module was doing at the time, dark and blank or showing its normal display. That one detail tells me whether the chip actually went into download mode, and it is the difference between chasing the buttons and chasing the data link. If it fails again, the exact error text as you sent it last time is perfect.

If it works, you will see the flasher count up through a percentage and then the module will reboot on its own. From there you connect it back to the BC04 and set up Wi-Fi and your pool, and I will walk you through that part when you get there.

JD, our hardware lead, has the error text and everything you have tried, and he picks it up today from 10am Eastern. If his answer lands before you are back at the PC, it will be waiting for you here. The Discord is also there any time at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, he is @nullhashrate.

Hal
